examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Choose a common unit or a convenient base such as 100 before comparing percentages. Track whether a percentage is of the whole population or a selected subgroup. For price problems distinguish number of items from their monetary contribution. Ratios of areas scale quadratically from linear similarity.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
Two items sell for 99 each, one at 10% profit and the other at 10% loss. What is the net loss percentage?

**Answer: 1.** Costs are 99/1.1=90 and 99/0.9=110, totaling 200. Receipts total 198, so loss is 2/200·100=1%. Equal percentage changes do not cancel for equal selling prices.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A rise of 20 percentage points is not necessarily a 20% relative increase. Specify the original denominator.

Applying a percentage to the wrong base can produce an apparently reasonable but incorrect answer.
